title: Rigveda 1.46: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.46: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.46 is a hymn of 15 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 31v-32r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.46.1-5 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 33); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 31v
translation.original_text:
1e̱ṣo u̱ṣā apū̍rvyā̱ vy u̍cchati pri̱yā di̱vaḥ | stu̱ṣe vā̍m aśvinā bṛ̱hat ||
2yā da̱srā sindhu̍mātarā mano̱tarā̍ rayī̱ṇām | dhi̱yā de̱vā va̍su̱vidā̍ ||
3va̱cyante̍ vāṁ kaku̱hāso̍ jū̱rṇāyā̱m adhi̍ vi̱ṣṭapi̍ | yad vā̱ṁ ratho̱ vibhi̱ṣ patā̍t ||
4ha̱viṣā̍ jā̱ro a̱pām pipa̍rti̱ papu̍rir narā | pi̱tā kuṭa̍sya carṣa̱ṇiḥ ||
5ā̱dā̱ro vā̍m matī̱nāṁ nāsa̍tyā matavacasā | pā̱taṁ soma̍sya dhṛṣṇu̱yā ||
translation.text:
1Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky: High, Aṣvins, I extol your praise,
2Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, ye Gods with deep thought who find out wealth.
3Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames, – When your car flies with winged steeds.
4He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant, Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full.
5Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nâsatyas, thinking of our words: Drink boldly of the Soma juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 31v (OPenn image 33, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.45.6 ‹-śociḥ-keśam puru-priya agne havyāya›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 32r, begins in RV 1.46.6 ‹yā naḥ pīparat aśvinā›. Verses 1.46.1-5 end on this page.

2yā | dasrā | sindhu-mātarā | manotarā | rayīṇām | dhiyā | devā | vasu-vidā
3vacyante | vām | kakuhāsaḥ | jūrṇāyām | adhi | viṣṭapi | yat | vām | rathaḥ | vi-bhiḥ | patāt
4haviṣā | jāraḥ | apām | piparti | papuriḥ | narā | pitā | kuṭasya | carṣaṇiḥ
5ādāraḥ | vām | matīnām | nāsatyā | mata-vacasā | pātam | somasya | dhṛṣṇu-yā

translation.original_ref: RV 1.46.6-15 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 3, varga 34); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 32r
translation.original_text:
6yā na̱ḥ pīpa̍rad aśvinā̱ jyoti̍ṣmatī̱ tama̍s ti̱raḥ | tām a̱sme rā̍sāthā̱m iṣa̍m ||
7ā no̍ nā̱vā ma̍tī̱nāṁ yā̱tam pā̱rāya̱ ganta̍ve | yu̱ñjāthā̍m aśvinā̱ ratha̍m ||
8a̱ritra̍ṁ vāṁ di̱vas pṛ̱thu tī̱rthe sindhū̍nā̱ṁ ratha̍ḥ | dhi̱yā yu̍yujra̱ inda̍vaḥ ||
9di̱vas ka̍ṇvāsa̱ inda̍vo̱ vasu̱ sindhū̍nām pa̱de | svaṁ va̱vriṁ kuha̍ dhitsathaḥ ||
10abhū̍d u̱ bhā u̍ a̱ṁśave̱ hira̍ṇya̱m prati̱ sūrya̍ḥ | vy a̍khyaj ji̱hvayāsi̍taḥ ||
11abhū̍d u pā̱ram eta̍ve̱ panthā̍ ṛ̱tasya̍ sādhu̱yā | ada̍rśi̱ vi sru̱tir di̱vaḥ ||
12tat-ta̱d id a̱śvino̱r avo̍ jari̱tā prati̍ bhūṣati | made̱ soma̍sya̱ pipra̍toḥ ||
13vā̱va̱sā̱nā vi̱vasva̍ti̱ soma̍sya pī̱tyā gi̱rā | ma̱nu̱ṣvac cha̍mbhū̱ ā ga̍tam ||
14yu̱vor u̱ṣā anu̱ śriya̱m pari̍jmanor u̱pāca̍rat | ṛ̱tā va̍natho a̱ktubhi̍ḥ ||
15u̱bhā pi̍batam aśvino̱bhā na̱ḥ śarma̍ yacchatam | a̱vi̱dri̱yābhi̍r ū̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
6Vouchsafe to us, O Aṣvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light, May through the darkness carry us.
7Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shore O Aṣvins, harness ye the car.
8The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waits Drops, with the hymn, have been prepared.
9Kaṇvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place: Where will ye manifest your form?
10Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold: And with its-tongue shone forth the dark.
11The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal: The road of heaven was manifest.
12The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Aṣvins give, who save when Soma gladdens them.
13Ye dwellers with Vivasvan come, auspicious, as to Manu erst; come to the Soma and our praise.
14O circumambient Aṣvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way: Approve with beams our solemn rites.
15Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Aṣvins Twain, With aids which none may interrupt.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 32r (OPenn image 33, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.46.6 ‹yā naḥ pīparat aśvinā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 32v, begins in RV 1.47.1 ‹-madhumat-tamaḥ sutaḥ somaḥ ṛta-vṛdhā›. Verses 1.46.6-15 end on this page.
